# SUMMONIC

> SUMMONIC is a text-to-audio instrument plugin. You describe an instrument in
> plain words and it generates a brand-new, fully playable sound inside your DAW,
> then lets you shape it and own it royalty-free. It runs as VST3, AU and AAX on
> macOS (Apple Silicon + Intel) and Windows x64. The plugin is a free download;
> generation runs on a monthly credit plan.

Site: https://summonic.ai
Maker: Producersources (https://producersources.com)

## What it does
- Generate original instruments from a text prompt (three variations per generation).
- Shape a generated clip into a playable instrument: loop, pitch-fix, stretch, glide.
- Finish the sound with a built-in rack: EQ, compressor, drive, chorus, tempo delay, reverb, modulation.
- Save results as searchable presets - your own growing sound library.
- Every sound is royalty-free and unique to you.

## Who it is for
Music producers, beatmakers and sound designers who want custom sounds without
digging through sample packs or programming synth patches.

## Pricing
- Free: download the plugin, 30 starter credits (about 10 generations).
- Starter $3.99/mo, Creator $7.99/mo, Pro $14.99/mo, Studio $29.99/mo.
- Each generation costs 3 credits and returns 3 options. Credits refresh monthly.
- Yearly plan codes are also sold on Producersources (2 months free), no auto-renew.

## Key pages
- Download (free): https://summonic.ai/download
- Plans & pricing: https://summonic.ai/plans
- Generate any instrument (use cases): https://summonic.ai/instruments
- Help & FAQ: https://summonic.ai/help

## Common questions
- Is it free? The plugin is free with starter credits; paid plans add monthly credits.
- Do I own the sounds? Yes, everything you generate is royalty-free and yours.
- Formats/OS? VST3, AU, AAX on macOS and Windows.
- Does it need internet? Yes, generation runs on a cloud GPU engine.

## Example prompts
"Warm analog Moog bass", "Long distorted 808 with a hard knock",
"Heavily distorted crunchy electric guitar with a sustained attack",
"Dusty lo-fi piano with vinyl crackle", "Dark trap bell, detuned".
